editorial.summary: Ed Piskor and Jim Rugg ask David Choe to reconstruct a concentrated comics week built around Brian K. Vaughan, Dave Mandel, private original-art collections and an unexpected invitation to interview Frank Miller at LA Comic Con. Choe explains how Slow Jams, Jordan Crane, SPX and Juxtapoz formed his early comics identity; recounts pandemic pitches to artists he admires; and describes collecting, provenance and stewardship through a private Mandel collection visit. A separate Kayfabe advertisement interrupts the conversation from about 14:41 to 17:08. The central panel story preserves Choe's fear of meeting a hero, his preparation, Jock's presence, bad stage acoustics, an invented abuse theory that Miller's answer contradicts, institutional conflict over Choe's variant covers, a disruptive fan, and Miller's direct refusal to discuss Lynn Varley's private life. Dinner produces non-dominant-hand and eyes-closed drawings, but not an announced collaboration. Choe's realization that the encounter is enough even if no project happens is the emotional center. The close unexpectedly supplies Ranch provenance: Choe says about four Ranch Solo DVDASA episodes were released from roughly twenty recordings. He then describes hiring Roddy Piper to perform the monologues, including masked anti-Asian improvisation Choe explicitly requested. Every idea remains. Private relationships, homes, collections, security, unreleased projects, unnamed people, hate speech and sexual imagery are controlled by contextual restrictions rather than deletion. Five duplicate caption pairs are removed only in the clean layer. No line-level speaker names are published.
